status.label: Compare local and forwarded picker input
status.detail: Remote keyboard failure is documented, but reports from other input-sharing tools leave Windows input handling as a competing cause.

next_action.label: Reproduce emoji-picker input boundary
next_action.reason: A two-PC comparison can distinguish PowerToys injection from a Windows picker focus/input restriction.

judgment.rationale: The title and numbered steps clearly identify remote keyboard input failing in the Windows 11 emoji picker. The Expected/Actual template text is reversed, so it is not used to invert the reported problem.
evidence: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/26702 supplies a two-PC reproduction on 0.70.1, with mouse input still working and even Escape rejected.
https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/26702#issuecomment-1579655328 reports the same symptom with Input Director and links 14328.
https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/26702#issuecomment-1581116059 reports Barrier behavior and suggests picker/process ownership.
The public timeline links duplicate reports 26747 and 27958 and tracking overview 51077, not a fix PR.
judgment.recommended_action: Run the supplied two-PC scenario and compare local, forwarded and post-selection input before choosing between a PowerToys key-injection correction and a Windows-owned limitation.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys-owned key representation or forwarding-state correction is possible but unconfirmed. Cross-tool reports prevent assuming that a module patch can resolve every case; no concrete fix attempt was identified.

proposed_fixes.title: Align forwarded key events with picker-compatible input semantics
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the emoji picker treats Mouse Without Borders synthesized key events differently from local hardware input, potentially because of scan-code/extended-key representation or picker focus state. A Windows-wide injected-input limitation is an equally material alternative.
plan: Compare local and forwarded letter, arrow and Escape input before and after selecting an emoji; include NumLock state because related 14328 reports picker-dependent differences.
Trace src/modules/MouseWithoutBorders/App/Class/InputSimulation.cs, especially key flag mapping and SendInputEx, and compare emitted event metadata with working local events.
Only if a PowerToys discrepancy is demonstrated, correct that event mapping or forwarding state while preserving extended keys, balanced key-up events and existing integrity/security boundaries.

Add regression coverage for the identified key representation and retest ordinary application input. If all equivalent injected paths fail, document the Windows boundary instead of adding a security-bypassing workaround.
verification: From PC A, open Win+. on Windows 11 PC B and test text, arrows and Escape while remote mouse input remains functional.
Compare the same keys locally on B and repeat after a mouse emoji selection and with NumLock toggled.
Verify any candidate does not break standard typing, modifiers, extended arrows or elevation boundaries.

confidence.rationale: The injection boundary is plausible and the relevant code exists, but multiple independent tools share the symptom and no event trace identifies a PowerToys defect.

issue_context.summary: On Windows 11, Mouse Without Borders forwards mouse input to the emoji picker but the picker rejects remote keyboard input, including Escape.
known_information: The original report uses two connected PCs, 0.70.1 and elevated PowerToys.
The description and title establish the failure despite swapped Expected/Actual fields.
Both comments discuss cross-tool reproduction; the related Keyboard Manager issue 14328 remains open and includes local picker/focus and NumLock observations.
The live issue is open, unassigned and has no linked fix PR.
inferences: A Windows picker/input path limitation is credible, but cross-tool similarity alone does not prove exclusive external ownership.
The related Keyboard Manager focus and NumLock observations are discriminators to test, not confirmed causes of this Mouse Without Borders report.
issue_context.analysis: The supplied steps support maintainer-side reproduction without asking the reporter to repeat basic configuration. Keep the fix hypothesis red until an event-path comparison identifies an actionable module discrepancy.
initial_investigation: Read the complete report and both comments, the full public cross-reference timeline and the related 14328 report/discussion.
Current InputSimulation.cs maps key-up/extended flags, obtains scan codes and calls SendInputEx, providing a concrete injection ownership lead.
Exact-number PR search found no match. Tracking issue 51077 is organizational related work, not a claimed implementation.

information_gaps.information: Whether only forwarded input fails and whether picker selection or NumLock changes that boundary on a current build.
information_gaps.why_needed: Separates a module-owned event mismatch from a Windows picker limitation.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Maintainer: execute the two-PC local/remote comparison and inspect emitted key metadata only if the current failure reproduces.

actions.label: Compare local and remote emoji-picker keys

reproduce.title: Mouse Without Borders Windows 11 emoji picker
reproduce.version_requirement: Current PowerToys build on both PCs; original report used 0.70.1.
prerequisites: Two trusted connected PCs, A and B, with Windows 11 on B.
Mouse Without Borders enabled and paired; a local keyboard on B for the control comparison.
steps: Move from A onto B and open Notepad to confirm ordinary forwarded typing works.
Open the emoji picker with Win+. or Win+; and test text search, arrows and Escape from A.
Without changing the active application, compare B's local keyboard and mouse input.
Reopen the picker, select an emoji with the mouse, then retry forwarded keys; repeat with NumLock off and on.
Record Windows build, PowerToys versions and service/elevation configuration; trace InputSimulation only if the failure persists.
reproduce.expected_result: Forwarded text/navigation/dismissal should behave like local input where Windows permits injection. Do not bypass secure-desktop or integrity restrictions to force parity.

actions.label: Approve scoped forwarded-input investigation
actions.note: Implementation remains conditional on demonstrating a PowerToys-owned discrepancy; no confirmed root cause or implementation-grade design is claimed.
